extracted.intended_audience: SEC staff, exchange regulators, market participants (Equity Members), and commenters on the proposed rule change
extracted.subtask_description: A Self-Regulatory Organization's (exchange) rule filing explaining and justifying proposed connectivity and port fees through cost allocation, projected revenues, competitive comparisons, and assessments of competitive impact. Intended to support SEC review and public comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid full allocation and double-counting of expenses
rubrics_metrics.description: The Exchange did not allocate any of its expenses in full to any core services (including physical connectivity or FIX and MEO Ports) and did not double-count any expenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instead, allocate applicable cost drivers across core services so that costs are apportioned according to usage/responsibility rather than fully assigned to a single service. The filing explains this principle and shows its application across human resources, depreciation, and other expense categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost-driver-based allocation of Human Resources expenses
rubrics_metrics.description: Human Resources expenses should be allocated based upon the function of employees and the degree to which their work supports each core service (e.g., network infrastructure personnel allocated 60% to 1Gb/10Gb ULL connectivity, 25% to FIX and MEO Ports, 15% to transactions and market data).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allocate HR costs across personnel groups in proportions reflecting primary job focus and support relationships; provide percent allocations and aggregate totals (e.g., total allocation of 47.6% of personnel costs to physical connections and 22.4% to FIX and MEO Ports). Explain when smaller allocations to other groups are used (e.g., 37% for certain specified personnel).

rubrics_metrics.name: Depreciation and amortization allocation based on equipment usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Allocate depreciation and amortization expense to core services in amounts tied to the actual cost of the computer equipment and network infrastructure purchased to operate and support the network (e.g., approximately 85% of overall depreciation/amortization attributed to connectivity services: 76.185% to 1Gb/10Gb ULL physical connections and 8.6% to FIX and MEO Ports).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain what assets are included (servers, monitors, security appliances, switches, taps, storage) and justify allocation percentages by showing how essential that equipment is to providing the connectivity services. Do not allocate all depreciation to connectivity; explicitly state remaining allocations to transactions, membership, and market data (approx. 15%).

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of general shared expenses to services that rely on them
rubrics_metrics.description: A portion of general shared expenses (office space, utilities, recruiting and training, marketing, professional fees, telecommunications, etc.) should be allocated to FIX and MEO Ports because without these general shared costs the Exchange would not be able to operate and provide application sessions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List what is included in general shared expenses and explain the allocation percentages used (e.g., overall 5.2% allocation of general shared expenses for FIX and MEO Ports; MIAX Pearl Equities allocated 1.20% to FIX Ports and 4.00% to MEO Ports). Justify higher allocations to services that require more in-house development and support (e.g., MEO) versus standardized solutions (e.g., FIX).

rubrics_metrics.name: Compute approximate per-unit cost by dividing allocated monthly cost by number of chargeable units
rubrics_metrics.description: Calculate approximate cost per FIX and MEO Port per month by dividing the total monthly cost allocated to each port type by the number of chargeable ports at the time pricing was determined (e.g., $76,000/142 = ~$535 per month per FIX Port; $253,333/336 = ~$754 per month per MEO Port).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Round to nearest dollar when dividing; explicitly show numerator (total monthly allocated cost) and denominator (number of chargeable units) used to derive per-unit costs so reviewers can reproduce the calculation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide projected revenue and compare to costs (profit margin analysis)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide annual cost estimates for each connectivity service and projected annual revenue based on current usage to show margins (e.g., 10Gb ULL: annual cost $17,726,799 vs. projected revenue ~$9,144,000; represents a negative margin).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present per-service cost and revenue projections, state whether margins are negative or positive, and explain assumptions/projections. Note that projections may change and will only be realized to the extent revenues materialize; include discussion of uncertainty and how changes in subscriber counts could affect outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benchmark fees against comparable fees charged by competing exchanges
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose rates that are comparable to, or lower than, similar fees for similar products charged by competing exchanges (examples: proposed 10Gb ULL fee lower than BX's $15,000/month and comparable to PSX's $7,500/month).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide specific comparator fee examples and argue that comparable/competitive pricing supports reasonableness even if resulting profit margins differ across exchanges due to different cost allocation methodologies or market structures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees should be reasonable, fair, equitable, and not unfairly discriminatory
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed fees are designed to align fees with services provided and will apply equally to all subscribers; they are equitably allocated among users of network connectivity and port alternatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how fee design and application ensure equitable allocation (e.g., first five ports provided free to each Equity Member) and that fees are applied uniformly regardless of participant size to avoid favoring categories of participants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocate fees according to resource consumption / usage intensity
rubrics_metrics.description: Fees should reflect the relative usage and resource consumption of different connection types (e.g., 10Gb ULL users consume substantially more bandwidth and account for more than 99% of message traffic while 1Gb users account for less than 1%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate how heavy users impose higher storage, surveillance, and network transport costs and therefore justify higher fees; use message traffic and capacity utilization metrics to support allocation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider intra-market competition and potential burdens
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether proposed fee changes will impose any burden on intra-market competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act; fees should not place certain market participants at a relative disadvantage or affect their ability to compete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss whether fees apply uniformly, whether they create barriers to participation for smaller firms, and whether the Exchange engaged informally with a diverse set of market participants when developing fees. Provide evidence or discussion of potential subscriber attrition and examples (e.g., a market maker terminated membership on another market due to fee changes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider inter-market competition and participant choice
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the proposed rule change will burden inter-market competition; recognize that market participants are free to choose other exchanges, route through other participants, or use resellers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain that there is no reason to believe the proposed price increase will harm another exchange's ability to compete and note alternative connectivity/resale options available to participants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commit to periodic review and update fees if necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: The Exchange commits to conduct a one-year review after implementation of these fees and to periodically review costs and subscribers to inform any future fee adjustments; any proposed fee change will include an updated cost estimate in the rule filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the intended review cadence (one-year review plus periodic reviews), the triggers for proposing increases or decreases (revenues failing to cover costs or revenue materially exceeding projections), and that updated analyses will be included in future filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for start-up/maturity phase when assessing reasonableness
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider the Exchange’s maturity phase (e.g., MIAX Pearl Equities commenced operations in 2020 and has operated at a cumulative net annual loss) and that new entrants may set low or zero initial fees to attract order flow; this context affects evaluation of proposed fees and margins.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain that start-ups may incur losses while building market share and that setting low fees initially is a competitive strategy; argue that proposed fee increases to recoup investment and cover increased costs are reasonable in that context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure participation remains affordable and avoid barriers to entry
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure that proposed pricing does not create a barrier to entry for smaller participants; availability of third-party providers and resellers helps maintain affordability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate that connectivity options and reseller markets provide alternatives for smaller firms, and show that fee structure (e.g., first five ports free, usage-based fees) supports accessibility for diverse participant sizes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Link fee design to correlated costs beyond direct connectivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that greater message traffic or number of connections increases related costs (e.g., storage, surveillance, service expenses) that, while not direct connection costs, are correlated and should be considered in fee design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe how increased messages/connections drive storage capacity purchases, surveillance program records, and other support costs; justify allocating portions of shared costs to connectivity for these correlated impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide transparent disclosure of analyses and advocate consistent regulatory standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide detailed cost analyses and projections; argue that Commission Staff should consider comparability, allocation methodologies, and be clear about what they deem an appropriate profit margin applied consistently across exchanges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supply supporting documentation, be transparent about assumptions and methodologies, and request clarity from regulators on margin standards (including consideration of allocation differences across affiliated vs. single-exchange operators).
